version: N11 scalar boundary selection and shift-invariant record v0.3
scope: Two N11 histories on the common canonical scalar quotient and the fixed centered scalar packet of v0.2. Treat scalar translations as a global action symmetry. Test effects commuting with that symmetry as a declared absence of an absolute field reference. This is not an additional CST constraint.
questions: Does the original scalar constraint force the two calibrated vacuum conditions?
Which linear boundary charges are transported identically by the two maps?
Can an invariant positive effect on one of the three inherited pairs give an unambiguous order record?
What balanced efficiency is achievable with all three modes, with an inconclusive outcome, for the same normed branch inputs?
Does this change either the inclusive density response or the clock contrast on the original dataset?
comparison: Branch-blind transport of a whole normal scalar state is examined as a separate, stronger candidate selection principle.
accuracy: Rational matrix and determinant tests, integer-root bounds for efficiencies, archived grid diagnostics for dust/clock probabilities. Conditional covariance and integrated overlap checked by an independent representation.
